seo_title: GenAI unit economics: the metric nobody tracks | Insight
meta_description: Cost per resolved task — not per token — is the real unit of GenAI economics.

blocks.x: Cost per resolved task — not per token — is the real unit of GenAI economics.

Why GenAI unit economics: the metric nobody tracks: because the differentiated advantage has moved to the data layer and the operating model around it. The technology is the commodity; the discipline is the moat.

items: Routing across model tiers cuts cost 40-60% at equal task quality on most workloads.
Distillation to right-sized models converts frontier quality into commodity cost.
Caching and prompt discipline matter more than model choice for high-volume flows.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: The failure mode is predictable: enthusiasm funds the demo, budget cycles gate the industrialization, and by the time the governance conversation starts, shadow usage has already created the exposure the review was meant to prevent.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: Programs we measure typically see serving cost per 1K tokens fall 50-70% after industrialization.
